acceptance: 1) Caller/wiring point: public App Router handlers -> composition.chat service. Real HTTP issues the seven-day idle/30-day absolute necessary cookie only for active contact; absent cookies do not recover old consultations. Return durable and unchanging id/seq/receivedAt only after the new conversation, first message, and messageId-unique outbox commit together. Same UUID/payload retries return the original result; changed payload returns 409 (E-16, E-18, E-31, E-85, E-90). 2) Exact Origin checks, size limiting before strict-schema parsing, and layered rate limits apply. email is optional; reject invalid/overlong/CRLF email. bodyText is plain text of 1..4000 code points. Store only a token hash; cookies contain no PII and do not depend on analytics consent. Another visitor's cookie cannot create or associate with someone else's thread (E-19, E-39, E-40). 3) A failed write leaves no partial conversation or outbox. Real PostgreSQL concurrency yields only one first message/notification. Successful consultation exchange advances 90-day retention; session polling does not. SMTP configuration does not affect received (E-18, E-86, E-90).

E-16.trigger: A visitor sends the first message while an operator is online.
E-16.expect: Persist the conversation and message before showing a received state. The operator inbox can read it and send a human reply; do not generate an automated AI answer.

E-18.trigger: The same message is submitted repeatedly because of retries.
E-18.expect: Deduplicate by the client message identifier so the inbox contains one message and notifications are not triggered repeatedly.

E-19.trigger: A visitor guesses another conversation identifier, or an unauthorized admin account accesses the inbox.
E-19.expect: Reject reads and replies. A visitor may access only their own conversation using their own unguessable session credential.

E-31.scene: C-01 Human inbox and reply entry points
E-31.trigger: A visitor submits a message and server-side persistence succeeds.
E-31.expect: Return stable conversation and message identifiers and show Received, with the conversation readable in the operator inbox. If the database write fails, retain a retry-pending state and do not show Received or read by an operator.

E-39.scene: C-02 Offline messages and recovery from send failures
E-39.trigger: The visitor voluntarily supplies a blank email, an invalid format, or overlong contact details.
E-39.expect: Mirror section 10: email is optional; when supplied, trim it, limit it to 254 characters, accept one valid mailbox, and reject display names and CRLF. Treat blank as omitted. Invalid or overlong values return field errors and retain the original message in the current tab. Do not elevate the email to verified identity or a delivery guarantee.

E-40.scene: C-02 Offline messages and recovery from send failures
E-40.trigger: A visitor declines analytics but actively opens first-party human chat.
E-40.expect: Allow the necessary consultation without creating an analytics identifier or loading a third-party chat script. Handle the necessary chat session separately from analytics consent.

E-85.trigger: The cookie reaches seven idle days or 30 days since issuance, or is revoked.
E-85.expect: The server rejects access to the old conversation using that credential; the browser may start a new consultation. Re-entering the same email alone cannot restore the old conversation. Neither the cookie nor any frontend copy stores PII.

E-86.trigger: A hidden tab still polls, or a visit merely refreshes without successfully sending or receiving a consultation message.
E-86.expect: These behaviors do not postpone the 90-day retention deadline for messages/email. Consultation activity means successfully persisted visitor messages or human replies; notification retries, delivery receipts, and read-state updates do not count as new consultation activity.

E-90.trigger: The process stops immediately after saving a message, or a client resends the same message following a timeout.
E-90.expect: Save the message and an outbox record unique by messageId in the same database transaction. Notifications for committed messages can continue after restart; a message-idempotency hit cannot create a second notification.
